headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors from ECC’s shared file/MCP surfaces; dbt-core’s warehouse-facing outputs can be misused downstream.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC reads/writes local files, uses MCP, and exposes stdin/stdout, so it can ingest dbt-core outputs if wired together. dbt-core emits warehouse-facing artifacts and documentation, which ECC may treat as workflow input. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from overlapping surfaces rather than observed interaction.
conditions: IF ECC is configured to consume dbt-core output files or stdout as instructions
IF both agents share a filesystem or MCP bridge
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Disable MCP routes that ingest untrusted text
Require manual review before ECC acts on dbt-core output
Use read-only mounts for dbt-core artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can call warehouse APIs, while ECC reads/writes local files and handles session summaries, hooks, and agent definitions. If dbt-core artifacts or warehouse-derived outputs are placed in ECC’s workspace, ECC can expose them through its broader file and API surfaces. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF warehouse-derived dbt artifacts are stored in ECC-accessible directories
IF ECC is allowed to upload or transmit those files through its APIs
mitigations: Keep warehouse outputs out of ECC-managed folders
Restrict ECC to non-sensitive projects
Turn off automatic file ingestion for sensitive directories
Review outbound API destinations before enabling sync
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call warehouse APIs, and ECC can execute shell, modify git state, write files, and use MCP. Both can mutate shared project state if pointed at the same repo or workspace, creating a realistic write/write conflict and possible irreversible git or file corruption. ECC’s concurrency notes explicitly warn about shared state across instances, increasing the likelihood of conflict.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF dbt-core writes generated artifacts while ECC modifies git or files concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a single operator
Pause ECC during dbt-core runs
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC has broad action-taking capabilities and can run browsers, shells, and subprocesses, so it may treat dbt-core outputs as authoritative and act on them. dbt-core produces data-modeling and documentation outputs that ECC could render or operationalize without verification. That creates a default pathway for incorrect upstream outputs to cascade into downstream actions.
conditions: IF ECC consumes dbt-core-generated artifacts without a verification step
IF ECC is configured to execute follow-on actions from those artifacts
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before actions
Require schema or test validation before use
Limit ECC to read-only summarization of dbt outputs
Flag dbt artifacts as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while ECC handles session summaries, metrics, hooks, and retention-related secrets. If warehouse data or regulated metadata flows into ECC’s retained session state, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is copied into ECC session summaries or retained files
IF retention settings keep those records longer than the source policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from session summaries
Shorten ECC retention for sensitive projects
Review retention settings before enabling sync
Store compliance-sensitive artifacts outside ECC
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
